real.Milestone: M3.1, no symbols. With the oracle's own 18 symbols supplied it is 0.9970/0.8579; ./build.sh Fidelity reports both. The ratchet is the without-symbols number because that is what `skala format` does with no project.

constructs.Milestone: M10, formatter tags: constructs/arrangement/formatter-tags/ adds three files to the set, taking it from 324 to 327. All three are byte-identical to CSReformatCode's answer, so the number rises rather than falls — which is the point of committing them: the oracle honours the tags under the format-only profile and ignores them under the cleanup profile (SK-DIV-0016), and the .arranged.expected.cs beside each of these is where that is pinned. M9 was 324 files at 0.9745/0.9228.

pathological.Milestone: ⚠ The one baseline in this file that has been LOWERED, and the argument is SK-DIV-0018. Four more fuzz reproductions were retired into the set (54 to 59): SK-FUZZ-0002's, -0003's, -0004's, and SK-FUZZ-0007's pair. Five of the six match the oracle byte for byte and raised the number to 0.9649/0.8966; mixed-line-endings-after-a-trailing-comment.cs then took it to 0.9589/0.8814 on its own. That file's three lines are SK-DIV-0018 entire — on a file whose endings are ALREADY mixed the oracle normalises the whole file to one ending and Skala keeps each gap's own, which is what `enforce_line_ending_style = false` says. It is not reachable on any internally consistent file, and crlf-throughout.cs and mixed-crlf-and-lf.cs are both still exact. ⚠ The alternative was to leave the reproduction out of the corpus, and that is the wrong instinct: docs/plan/12 says the corpus only grows, the pathological set exists to hold the files that are hard, and a minimised reproduction dropped because it embarrasses a number is a measurement managing its own result. M10 was 54 files at 0.9636/0.8889.

preservation/keep-keep.Milestone: M3.1 - `keep_existing_expr_member_arrangement` now outranks the placement key in both directions, the same way a delimited list's does. M3 was 0.9086/0.7692.

preservation/keep-rearrange.Milestone: M3 - keep_user_linebreaks=true, keep_existing_*=false; the corner that costs a first-run diff, and now exact. M2 was 0.8765.

preservation/reflow-rearrange.Milestone: M3 - keep_user_linebreaks=false, keep_existing_*=false (--reflow), and now exact. M2 was 0.8844.

unformatted/scramble.Milestone: The unformat differential, first measurement (⚠ corpus/real/'s own null hypothesis, for scale, is 0.9095/0.2684): 380 files of corpus/real/ with their formatting scrambled - indentation randomised, one line break in three moved to a legal-but-wrong place, blank lines added and removed. ⚠ Its own population, beside the corpus/real/ number rather than replacing it; the two differentials ask different questions of different inputs. The null hypothesis on this population is 0.3073/0.0000, so the gap this closes is 48.3 % of the line gap available - read that beside the number, not the number alone. ⚠ 204 of the 380 files are dominated by one defect: a file-scoped namespace whose name is wrapped makes Skala indent the whole rest of the file. Those score 0.3800 and the other 176 score 0.8893, so fixing it should take this entry to roughly 0.89 rather than to 0.65.

unformatted/collapse.Milestone: The unformat differential, first measurement (⚠ corpus/real/'s own null hypothesis, for scale, is 0.9095/0.2684): the same 380 files with every line break the language does not force removed, so both tools build the layout from nothing. Null hypothesis 0.3238/0.0000; 87.8 % of the available line gap closed. ⚠ Higher than scramble's 0.6418 and that is the finding rather than a surprise - reflowing from nothing is the easier problem, and agreeing about which of the author's breaks to keep is the one that runs in production.
